scenes.title: TLS 1.3 handshake and certificate validation
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains tls 1.3 handshake and certificate validation by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Follow the four numbered stages. The client sends ClientHello with supported ciphers and an ephemeral key share. The server selects parameters, sends its key share and authenticates using a certificate and related handshake messages. The client validates the hostname, certificate chain, validity dates and trusted certificate authority; an invalid certificate should reject the connection. Both peers derive traffic keys from the negotiated shared secret and use them for encrypted application messages.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Protocol policy, genuine server authentication and endpoint validation are each essential.

scenes.title: ACM public certificate lifecycle
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains acm public certificate lifecycle by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The first box requests a certificate for a public domain; the next validates ownership using DNS records. Once issued, the certificate is attached to a compatible Application Load Balancer or CloudFront distribution. The fourth step concerns renewal: eligible Amazon-issued public certificates can renew automatically when validation and other requirements remain satisfied. CloudFront certificate integration requires ACM in us-east-1. Imported certificates need separate replacement and renewal operations.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Verify the certificate is deployed in the correct Region and that renewal is actually functioning.

scenes.title: AWS Private CA and private trust
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains aws private ca and private trust by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Start with the CA hierarchy: a root CA can issue subordinate CAs, and access to their signing capabilities must be restricted. Follow the central certificate issuance path to an internal service. The service presents its private certificate during TLS, while internal clients must trust the appropriate CA root or chain distributed to their trust stores. The right panels show certificate renewal, revocation and monitoring. Public browsers do not automatically trust these private certificates, and revocation-check behavior varies by client.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Certificate issuance without trust distribution and lifecycle management does not provide reliable private authentication.
